Rashi on Arakhin 31b:10:1.hebrew: לא כתב תמימה - ולא ליתיב ליה חדש העיבור, וליסלקיה שנה בט"ו בשבט:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:10:1.english: [Where] "full" is not written - and [therefore] one would not give it the intercalated month, and its year would be completed on the fifteenth of Shevat:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:11:1.english: In accordance with the number of days of the solar [year] - whether in an ordinary [year] or in an intercalated [year]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:11:2.hebrew: י"ב חדש מיום ליום - כמו שאנו קובעין אותן לשנת לבנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:11:2.english: Twelve months from day to day - As we establish them for a lunar year:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:11:3.english: [It] was intercalated for him - [That is,] for the seller, as it is written: "[a] full [year]":

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:13:1.hebrew: האמר - במס' בכורות בפ' אחרון (דף נב:), מתנה אינה כמכר לחזור ביובל למי שנתנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:13:1.english: Doesn’t he say - in Tractate Bekhorot, in the last chapter (52b), [that] a gift is not like a sale to return in the Jubilee [Year] to the one who gave it:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:14:1.hebrew: תשובו - "תשובו איש אל אחוזתו", ודרשינן (בפ"ט) (שם) לרבות את המתנה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:14:1.english: You shall return - "You shall return, each man unto his possession" [Leviticus 25:13], and we expound (in chapter 9, there) [that it serves] to include a gift:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:15:1.hebrew: וגואל לעולם - שאינו נחלט להקדש לעולם, ולקמן מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:15:1.english: And he may redeem [it] forever - [Meaning] that it is never permanently forfeited to the Temple treasury, and below [the Gemara] explains the reason:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:15:2.english: The day of the twelve months arrived - [counted] from when he acquired it from the [Temple] treasurer:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:16:1.english: As it does not have generations - For there is no procreation before Heaven:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:17:1.english: "It shall not go out in the Jubilee" — why do I [need it]? - Since it is written "in perpetuity":

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:18:1.hebrew: היה נטמן - הלוקח ביום שנים עשר חודש, כדי שלא ימצאהו מוכר ליתן לו מעותיו, והוא חלוט לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:18:1.english: He would conceal himself - [i.e.,] the buyer, on the [final] day of the twelve-month [period], so that the seller would not find him to give him his money, and [thus] it [the house] becomes permanently his:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:18:2.hebrew: שיהא חולש - כמו (ישעיהו י״ד:י״ב) "חולש על גוים", וכדגרסינן (שבת דף קמח:) "מטילין חלשים על הקדשים", שיהא מטיל מעותיו ללשכות שבעזרה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:18:2.english: That he would cast [ḥolesh] - As [in] (Isaiah 14:12), "who casts [lots] [ḥolesh] upon the nations," and as we learn (Shabbat 148b), "they cast lots [ḥalashim] upon the consecrated offerings" — [meaning] that he would cast his money into the chambers in the Temple Courtyard:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:18:3.english: And he may break the door - of the house that he sold, and enter [it]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:19:1.english: With his consent - [meaning] that he accepts them willingly:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:19:2.hebrew: בעל כרחו - שהטילתם בביתו, כי ה"ג דתקין הלל במתני':
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:19:2.english: Against his will - [meaning] that she threw them [the coins] into his house, in the manner that Hillel instituted in the Mishnah:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:1:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא צד אחד ברבית - כי ה"ג אסור, הואיל ומעיקרא בתורת הלואה אתא לידיה. ור' יהודה (דקאמר) [דקשרי] — בהכי עסקינן, שהתנו מתחילה שאם יגאלנה המוכר בתוך שלש, יחזיר לו הלוקח הדמים מפירות שאכל, וברבית ע"מ להחזיר פליגי. ומתני' ותנא דברייתא בהא פליגי: דתנא דידן סבר אפי' צד אחד נמי לא הוי, דהא בתורת מכר אתא לידיה; ותנא דברייתא סבר סוף סוף הואיל ולידי ריבית (לגבי) [אתי], צד אחד (היא) כרבית גמורה היא, אלא שהתורה התירתה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:1:1.english: Everyone [agrees that] one-sided interest - in such a case is prohibited, since originally it came into his hand as a loan. And [as for] Rabbi Yehudah who permits [it] — we are dealing here with [a case] where they stipulated from the outset that if the seller redeems it within three [years], the buyer will return to him the value of the produce that he ate, and they disagree regarding interest [taken] on condition of returning [it]. And our Mishnah and the Tanna of the Baraita disagree about this: for our Tanna holds [that] it is not even one-sided [interest], since it came into his hand as a sale; whereas the Tanna of the Baraita holds [that] ultimately, since it comes to interest, one-sided [interest] is like full-fledged interest, except that the Torah permitted it:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:2:1.english: (“If a man sells,” the Merciful One states):

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:2:2.hebrew: והיתה גאולתו מ"מ - משמע, דא"כ הוה ליה למיכתב "יגאלנה עד תום שנת ממכרו"; מדשני בדיבוריה וכתב "והיתה גאולתו", משמע אפי' ע"י אחר:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:2:2.english: And he shall have the right of redemption, in any case - [The verse] implies [this], for if it were so [that only the seller could redeem], it should have written, "he shall redeem it until the completion of the year of its sale"; since it changed its phrasing and wrote, "and he shall have the right of redemption," it implies even through another [person]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:3:1.hebrew: לקונה אותו - משמע: לקונה יהא נחלט אם לא יגאל בתוך שנה, הא אם יגאל יחזירנה, וקונה הוא דיחזירנה, אבל בנו לא; קמ"ל "והיתה גאולתו" מ"מ:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:3:1.english: To the one who bought it - [This] implies: to the buyer it shall become permanently his if it is not redeemed within a year, whereas if it is redeemed, he shall return it; and it is [specifically] the buyer who must return it, but not his son. [Therefore, the verse] teaches us: "he shall have the right of redemption" — in any case:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:4:1.hebrew: שנה - אי הוה כתיב "עד מלאת שנה" ולא כתב "לו", איני יודע אם שנה למכר ראשון או שנה למכר שני — כגון מכרה ראובן לשמעון בניסן, ושמעון ללוי בתשרי, וה"א: ראובן שמכרה ראשון מחשב עם לוי, ויהא לו רשות לגאלה עד תשרי הבא; השתא דכתיב "לו", משמע דאמוכר ראשון קא מהדר:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:4:1.english: Year - If it were written "until the passage of a year" and it had not written "for him," I would not know whether [it means] a year from the first sale or a year from the second sale — for example, [if] Reuven sold it to Shimon in Nisan, and Shimon [sold it] to Levi in Tishrei, and I would have said [that] Reuven, who sold it first, calculates [the year] with Levi, and he would have permission to redeem it until the coming Tishrei; now that "for him" is written, it implies that it refers back to the first seller:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:5:1.hebrew: למי חלוט - כשהגיע שנה למוכר ראשון ונחלט, מי מן הלוקחים זוכה בחליטה זו:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:5:1.english: To whom [does it belong] in perpetuity? - When a year has arrived for the first seller and it becomes irredeemable, which of the buyers acquires this permanent title:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:5:2.hebrew: לראשון חלוט - דראובן אין גואלה עוד משמעון, אבל שמעון גואלה מלוי עד שיגיע שנה למכר שני, שהרי ללוי לא נחלטה:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:5:2.english: To the first [buyer it belongs] in perpetuity - For Reuven [the original owner] can no longer redeem it from Shimon [the first buyer], but Shimon can redeem it from Levi [the second buyer] until a year arrives from the second sale, since it has not become permanent for Levi:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:5:3.english: [It belongs] in perpetuity to the second [buyer] - [Meaning] that Shimon [the first buyer] cannot redeem it from Levi [the second buyer]:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:6:1.hebrew: עלתה לו שנה - דהאיכא מיום ליום, וזה שמכר לו בט"ו באדר לא עלתה לו שנה עד ט"ו באדר לשנה הבאה, ואע"ג דהשתא הוו י"ג חדש, משום דמיום ליום בעינן — מט"ו באדר לט"ו באדר:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:6:1.english: It is counted as a year - since there is [a full year] from day to day. And [as for] this [house] that he sold to him on the fifteenth of Adar [I], it is not counted as a year for him until the fifteenth of Adar of the next year, even though now there are thirteen months, because we require [a full year] from day to day — from the fifteenth of Adar to the fifteenth of Adar:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:7:1.hebrew: ולימא ליה - לוקח ראשון ללוקח שני: "אנא קדים שחין נורא" — אני היסקתי ונשתמשתי בבית קודם ממך, ושלך נחלט באחד באדר, ושלי לא תיחלט:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:7:1.english: And let him say to him - The first buyer [says] to the second buyer: "I preceded [you and] kindled a fire" — I kindled [a fire] and made use of the house before you, and [yet] yours becomes permanently acquired on the first of Adar, while mine does not become permanently acquired:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:7:2.hebrew: את נחתת לעיבורא - נכנסת בחודש העיבור, לפיכך תפסיד, ד"תמימה" כתיב, ליתן לו חדש העיבור, אבל אני לא נכנסתי בו:
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:7:2.english: You descended to the intercalated [month] - You entered [into possession] during the intercalated month; therefore you will lose [out], for "full" is written [regarding a year], to give him [the seller] the intercalated month, whereas I did not enter [into possession] during it:

Rashi on Arakhin 31b:8:1.hebrew: נולדו לו שני טלאים - והם בכורות, ומוזהר להקריבן בתוך שנתן, דכתיב (דברים טו): "תאכלנו שנה בשנה":
Rashi on Arakhin 31b:8:1.english: Two lambs were born to him - And they are firstborn [animals], and he is admonished to sacrifice them within their [first] year, as it is written (Deuteronomy 15): "You shall eat it year by year":

Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:13:1.hebrew: דאי ר"מ הא אמר מתנה אינה כמכר - י"ל דכיון דאינה כמכר, אין בידו לגואלה לעולם, אפי' תוך י"ב חדש. ולפי זה, מה שהקשינו בפ' המקדיש (לעיל ערכין כח:), כיון דכתיב "אחוזת עולם היא להם", היה לנו לומר שלא יתנו בתיהם במתנה. אבל נוכל לפרש הכא דמתנה אינה כמכר, ויכול הנותן לגאול לעולם, אפי' אחר י"ב חדש; ובהכי ניחא, דיכולים כהנים ולוים ליתן לאחר בתיהם במתנה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:13:1.english: For if [it is] Rabbi Meir, doesn’t he say [that] a gift is not like a sale - One can say that since [a gift] is not like a sale, [the giver] does not have the ability to redeem it ever, even within twelve months. And according to this, [with respect to] what we asked in the chapter [entitled] Hamakdish (above, Arakhin 28b) — since it is written, "it is an eternal possession for them," we should have said that they may not give their houses as a gift. However, we can explain here that a gift is not like a sale, and the giver can redeem [it] forever, even after twelve months; and with this it is well, that priests and Levites can give their houses to another as a gift:

Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:18:1.hebrew: התקין הלל - הכא משמע דבימי הלל, שהיה בבית שני — כדאמרינן בפ"ק דשבת (דף טו. ושם): "הלל ושמעון גמליאל ושמעון נהגו נשיאותן לפני הבית מאה שנה" — היו נוהגין יובל, כיון דבתי ערי חומה היה נוהג, כדאמר בפירקין דלעיל (ערכין דף כט.) דאין בתי ערי חומה אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג. וקשה לפירש"י דפרק השולח (גיטין דף לו.), דתנן: "הלל תיקן פרוזבול", ופריך בגמ' עלה: "מי איכא מידי דאורייתא משמטא והתקין הלל דלא תשמט?", ומשני: "בשביעית בזמן הזה דרבנן", ופרש"י: והלל כרבי סבירא ליה, דאמר שביעית להשמטת מלוה בזמן הזה דרבנן, ואע"ג דהלל בבית שני הוה, סבירא ליה דבבית שני הואיל ולא היה יובל נוהג, לא היה נוהג שמיטה מדאורייתא, ודאמרינן "מנו יובלות לקדש שמיטין", מדרבנן קאמר. וכאן משמע דבבית שני היה יובל נוהג מן התורה! וכן משמע בכריתות פרק ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה בסופו (דף יא.): "'ויתנו ידיהם להוציא (את) נשיהם ואשמים' וגו' — אמר רב חסדא: מלמד שכולן שפחה חרופה בעלו"; ושפחה חרופה היינו חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין המאורסת לעבד עברי, ואמרינן בפרקין דלעיל (ערכין דף כט.) דאין עבד עברי נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג, אלמא נהגו יובלות בבית שני! וצ"ל דע"כ דאין הכי נמי דנהגו יובלות בבית שני, ואע"ג דכל ישראל לא חזרו בימי עזרא, כדכתיב (נחמיה ז׳:ס״ו): "כל הקהל כאחד ארבע רבוא אלפים שלש מאות וששים", ומיהו מכל שבט ושבט חזרו מקצתן, והוי שפיר כמו "כל יושביה עליה", כדאמרינן לקמן שמנו יובלות אע"ג דלא חזרו כולן. וההיא דפרק השולח (גיטין דף לו.) צ"ל דהלל לאו לדריה תקין, אלא יודע היה שהבית היה עתיד ליחרב ולפיכך תיקן פרוזבול. ואע"ג דבעי התם: "הלל כי תקין פרוזבול לדריה הוא דתקין או לדרי עלמא תקין?", ההיא לאו לאביי קבעי, כי אם לרבא, דמתרץ התם: "הפקר ב"ד היה הפקר":
Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:18:1.english: Hillel instituted - Here it is implied that in the days of Hillel, who lived during the Second Temple [era] — as we say in the first chapter of Shabbat (15a and there): "Hillel and Shimon, Gamliel and Shimon, held their office of Nasi during the [last] hundred years before the [destruction of the] Temple" — they observed the Jubilee, since [the law of] houses in walled cities was in force, as [the Gemara] stated in our chapter above (Arakhin 29a) that [the law of] houses in walled cities applies only at a time when the Jubilee is in force. And this is difficult according to Rashi's explanation in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 36a), where we learned in the Mishnah: "Hillel instituted prosbul," and the Gemara asks on it: "Is there anything that by Torah law is remitted, and Hillel instituted that it should not be remitted?" And it answers: "[It refers to] the Sabbatical year in the present era, which is rabbinic." And Rashi explained: Hillel holds like Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says that the Sabbatical year with respect to the remission of loans in the present era is rabbinic; and even though Hillel lived during the Second Temple [era], he held that during the Second Temple [era], since the Jubilee was not in force, the Sabbatical year was not in force by Torah law, and that which we say [elsewhere], "They counted Jubilees in order to sanctify Sabbatical years," refers to a rabbinic [observance]. Yet here it is implied that during the Second Temple [era], the Jubilee was in force by Torah law! And so too it is implied in Keritot at the end of the chapter [entitled] Arba'a Meḥussarei Kappara (11a): "'And they gave their hands to send away their wives, and [offered] guilt-offerings, etc.' — Rav Ḥisda said: This teaches that they all had intercourse with a betrothed maidservant [shifḥa ḥarufa]"; and a shifḥa ḥarufa is [a woman who is] half-slave and half-free who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave, and we say in our chapter above (Arakhin 29a) that [the law of] a Hebrew slave is in force only when the Jubilee is in force — thus [proving that] they observed Jubilees during the Second Temple [era]! And one must say that perforce it is indeed so that they observed Jubilees during the Second Temple [era], and even though not all of Israel returned in the days of Ezra, as it is written (Nehemiah 7:66): "The whole congregation together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty," nevertheless some from each and every tribe returned, and it is properly considered like "all its inhabitants upon it," as we say later [in our tractate] that they counted Jubilees even though not all of them returned. And [regarding] that passage in the chapter [entitled] HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 36a), one must say that Hillel did not institute [prosbul] for his own generation, rather he knew that the Temple was destined to be destroyed and therefore he instituted prosbul. And even though [the Gemara] asks there: "When Hillel instituted prosbul, did he institute it for his own generation or did he institute it for [all] generations of the world?", that [question] was not asked according to Abaye, but rather according to Rava, who answers there: "What is declared ownerless by the court is ownerless":

Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:1:1.hebrew: רבא אמר דכולי עלמא צד אחד ברבית אסור - פירש"י: "ומתני' וברייתא בהא פליגי, דתנא דברייתא סבר: סוף סוף, הואיל ולידי הרבית (לגבי) [אתי], צד אחד ברבית וכרבית גמורה היא, אלא שהתורה התירתו", [לשון] רש"י. ועוד יש לפרש, דבהכי פליגי מתני' וברייתא: כגון שנכנס בבית להחזיר לו דמי שכירות שנה אם בא לפדותו בתוך י"ב חדש, דתנא דמתני' סבר רבית על מנת להחזיר שרי, ותנא דברייתא סבר דאסור. אי נמי, מר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי, דמתני' מיירי כשמחזיר לו אם יפדנו, וברייתא מיירי כשאין מחזיר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 31b:1:1.english: Rava said: Everyone [agrees that] uncertain interest is prohibited - Rashi explained: "And the Mishnah and the baraita disagree about this, for the tanna of the baraita holds: Ultimately, since it comes to interest, [it is] uncertain interest and is like full-fledged interest, except that the Torah permitted it" — [the] language of Rashi. And one can also explain that the Mishnah and the baraita disagree about this: [for example,] a case where [the buyer] entered the house [on condition] to return to him the rental fee for a year if [the seller] comes to redeem it within twelve months; for the tanna of the Mishnah holds [that] interest [given] on the condition that it will be returned is permitted, and the tanna of the baraita holds that it is prohibited. Alternatively, one [tanna] said one [case] and one [tanna] said another [case], and they do not disagree: for the Mishnah is speaking of when he returns [it] to him if he redeems it, and the baraita is speaking of when he does not return [it]:
